claims.text: A hybrid DSC, in situ STEM-heating, and calibrated atomistic-simulation approach can accurately determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, melting volume change, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the HEA family.
Thermodynamic mixing parameters such as ΔS_mix, ΔH_mix, atomic-size mismatch δ, and Ω can serve as predictive levers for HEA melting and liquid properties.
The protocol is intended for HEAs that are predominantly single-phase solid solutions or are in well-characterized multiphase states before melting.
The proposed protocol combines DSC, in situ STEM heating, and molecular-dynamics simulation calibrated for HEA compositional and structural complexity.
Experiments should use controlled heating rates and consistent atmospheres, with simulations following the same thermal ramp.
The protocol applies across alloys with at least five elemental components, including AuCoCuNiPt and AlCoFeNi variants.
Testing multiple alloys under matched experimental and simulated ramps captures both equilibrium and kinetic effects.
High mixing entropy and atomic-size mismatch mediate atomic mixing and diffusion behavior, thereby affecting phase stability and melting phenomena.
Mixing enthalpy, mixing entropy, and atomic-size mismatch influence HEA phase stability.
DSC is sensitive to thermal events associated with melting.
In situ STEM heating can capture microstructural, structural, and chemical evolution during HEA heating.
Calibration with molecular-dynamics simulations enables the integrated method to account for both thermodynamic and kinetic influences on melting.
The integrated method will determine melting temperatures within ±10 K of calibrated standards.
The integrated method will determine fusion enthalpy and fusion entropy within ±5% of calibrated standards.
Melting volume changes and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties will be quantified with accuracies similar to those claimed for temperature, enthalpy, and entropy.
Kinetic nonequilibrium effects or extreme phase separation can reduce the method's effectiveness and cause errors beyond the stated tolerances.
Uncertainty in mapping MD simulations to experimental conditions and variation in microstructural evolution may alter DSC signals and limit generalization across HEAs.

contradictions.description: The stated applicability requires at least five elemental components, but AlCoFeNi is offered as an example even though the named parent alloy contains only four elements; unspecified 'variants' do not resolve the scope unambiguously.
